claim_text: Omega-3 supplements can affect platelet function, but evidence does not support treating ordinary omega-3 intake as an automatic bleeding contraindication for everyone; high-dose use, anticoagulant/antiplatelet therapy, bleeding disorders and perioperative context require individualized review.
health_goal_or_outcome: Assess bleeding and perioperative context before recommending algal EPA/DHA.

population.age_range: Adults; specific groups require individualized review.
population.sex_or_life_stage: All life stages; pregnancy requires separate assessment.
population.health_status: People with bleeding disorders, taking antithrombotic medicines or undergoing surgery.
population.other_context: Actual EPA/DHA dose and product composition matter.

ingredient_form_or_preparation: Algal DHA or EPA/DHA supplements; verify EPA and DHA amounts separately.
evidence_summary: NIH ODS Omega-3 Health Professional Fact Sheet summarizes bleeding-related safety evidence and medication context.
limitations: Do not generalize findings across all doses and formulations.
Do not stop prescribed antithrombotic therapy.
Perioperative decisions belong to the treating clinician.
